To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) most people (including older people) like voices with medium intensity and fundamental frequency (F0) values, and (2) there are no significant differences in voice preference between older and younger people.

(a) the preferred voice type for older listeners is the medium-intensity, medium-pitch, male voice; (b) there is no significant change in preferences with increasing age; and (c) there are no differences between male and female preferences.

older adults prefer medium intensity voices; they prefer low-pitched voices slightly more than higher-pitched voices; they prefer male voices slightly more than female voices; and they prefer male voices with low fundamental frequencies and high intensities.
